resources.string: Radius and ulna with the palm facing forward
Radial head
The disc-shaped head at the elbow can turn against the ulna when you rotate the forearm.
Radial shaft
The shaft runs along the thumb side in this view. The fibrous sheet between the two bones connects their shafts.
Wrist end
The widened distal radius meets part of the first row of wrist bones.
Radial styloid
This bony projection marks the thumb side of the wrist.
Olfactory mucosa, enlarged section · not to scale
Mucus film
Odor molecules enter the thin wet layer at the mucosal surface before encountering receptors on sensory cilia.
Olfactory cilia
These extensions of olfactory neurons reach into the mucus. They detect odors; they do not sweep mucus like the motile cilia elsewhere in the nose.
Supporting cells
These epithelial cells surround the sensory neurons and help maintain the tissue around them.
Olfactory gland
A gland below the epithelium delivers its secretion to the surface through a small duct.
Cranial nerve connections viewed from below · schematic
I · Olfactory
Olfactory nerve fibers from the nasal mucosa enter the bulbs on the underside of the forebrain.
II · Optic
The optic nerves from the two eyes meet at the optic chiasm, where some fibers cross.
III and IV · Midbrain
The oculomotor nerve (III) appears on the underside of the midbrain. The trochlear nerve (IV) emerges on the back and curves around the side, indicated by broken lines.
V · Trigeminal
The main trigeminal root is attached along the lateral pons. It carries much of the sensation of the face and contributes to chewing movements.
VI–VIII · Pons border
At the pons–medulla border, abducens (VI) is near the midline; facial (VII) and vestibulocochlear (VIII) attach farther to the side.
IX and X · Medulla
Glossopharyngeal (IX) and vagus (X) have small roots along the side of the medulla.
XI · Accessory
The main spinal component rises alongside the upper cervical spinal cord rather than emerging from the pons.
XII · Hypoglossal
Hypoglossal rootlets emerge from a groove closer to the midline of the medulla. The nerve supplies most tongue muscles.
Upper and lower limb bones · side-by-side schematic
Hair shaft and its layers · magnified
Cuticle
Overlapping flattened cells form the thin outer layer that protects the shaft.
Cortex
This thick middle layer contains keratin fibers that give the shaft much of its strength.
Medulla
A central region that can be continuous, interrupted or absent. It is shown in this example.
